# czc-v2026.10.22.2 (0.2.17.19)

OAuth-only Codex request synthesis. Generic Responses, Chat Completions, and
Anthropic Messages traffic routed to an OpenAI OAuth account is rebuilt into the
Codex CLI request shape, while SetupToken, API-key, and non-OpenAI traffic keeps
the previous byte-for-byte path.

## Changes since czc-v2026.10.22.1

### Request synthesis

- **OAuth-only full synthesis.** Generic clients on OpenAI OAuth accounts are
  rebuilt into the Codex CLI request shape: the official base prompt as
  `input[0]`, permissions/skills/environment context, official hosted tools,
  and stable `client_metadata` identities. SetupToken, API-key, and non-OpenAI
  accounts never enter this path (`gateway.codex_full_synthesis`, default
  `true`).
- **Official tools.** `exec_command`, `apply_patch`, `view_image`, and
  `write_stdin` schemas come from the 0.163 golden capture; client tool aliases
  are mapped both ways. The native capability (`model.base_instructions`) keeps
  the base prompt without re-synthesizing it.
- **Context budget.** Optional skill/permissions blocks are trimmed first; the
  base prompt and actual client input are never silently truncated.
- **Prompt cache key.** Defaults to the mapped session id for full/session
  profiles; messages-bridge bodies omit it.

### Device and wire profiles

- **Account-level device profiles.** OAuth accounts can pin
  `codex_client_family` (`tui`/`exec`/`vscode`), `codex_platform_profile`,
  `codex_sandbox`, `codex_sandbox_mode`, `codex_workspace_cwd`, and
  `codex_timezone`. The same UA/originator is used for HTTP, WS, plugin
  identity, quota calls, and OAuth token refresh. `force_codex_cli` still pins
  the canonical TUI identity.
- **Version profiles.** `gateway.codex_wire.profile` selects the 0.163
  (`stable`) or 0.164 (`main`) wire behavior; `auto` follows the synced Codex
  version. `gateway.codex_wire.strict` rejects unknown future versions while
  synthesizing; a pinned `stable` profile keeps working.
- **0.164 behavior.** Non-lite models clear per-item
  `content_item_metadata`, adjacent `configuration_update` items are deduped
  keeping the latest, and `prompt_cache_key` follows the
  `SessionDerived`/`Custom`/`Omit` policy (`codex_prompt_cache_key_policy` in
  account Extra).

### Wire closure

- HTTP synthesized bodies emit the official `ResponsesApiRequest` top-level key
  order. `client_metadata` keys are deterministically shuffled per
  turn/session, and the HTTP/WS shared-key relative order stays consistent
  (`gateway.codex_wire.map_order_jitter`, default `true`).
- OAuth Codex extra client headers (subagent, parent thread, memgen, timing
  metrics) are forwarded only when the client actually sent them.
- The OAuth Codex SSE idle timeout defaults to 300s
  (`gateway.codex_wire.stream_idle_timeout_seconds`, default `300`; an explicit
  `0` falls back to `gateway.stream_data_interval_timeout`).
- OAuth token refresh, quota calls, and plugin identity use the account device
  UA. Invalid device Extra is stripped on save instead of rejecting the account.

### Model catalog

- The official `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` is pinned and embedded
  (`backend/internal/pkg/openai/codex_catalog_models.json`, hash asserted).
  `gpt-5.6-*`, `gpt-6-sol/luna`, `gpt-daybreak-*`, and `codex-auto-review` now
  resolve real prompts instead of falling back to GPT-5.5.
- The stable 0.163 profile uses the captured `gpt-5.5` base prompt
  (`instructions_gpt5_5_0_163.txt`); `tools/codexprompts` refreshes and prints
  the catalog hash.

### Golden tooling

- `codexgolden compare -golden <dir> -candidate <dir>` reports header order,
  body top-level order, and TLS ClientHello drift.

## VERSION

`0.2.17.19`

## Upgrade guidance

Drop-in, no database migration. All new switches default to the behavior
described above; an explicit value in `config.yaml` wins.

| Key | Default | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway.codex_full_synthesis` | `true` | Set `false` for the legacy pass-through. |
| `gateway.codex_wire.profile` | `auto` | `stable` pins 0.163, `main` pins 0.164. |
| `gateway.codex_wire.strict` | `false` | `true` rejects unknown future versions while synthesizing. |
| `gateway.codex_wire.map_order_jitter` | `true` | `false` restores the fixed `client_metadata` order. |
| `gateway.codex_wire.stream_idle_timeout_seconds` | `300` | `0` falls back to `gateway.stream_data_interval_timeout`. |

## Compatibility

- `codex_full_synthesis` and `codex_wire.*` are ignored for SetupToken,
  API-key, and non-OpenAI platform accounts.
- Existing per-account UA overrides still win over the device profile.
- A nil or hand-built `config.Config{}` keeps synthesis and jitter off; only
  viper-loaded production config enables them.
- `codex_cli_only` still rejects generic clients even with synthesis enabled.

## Rollback

Redeploy the previous `czc-*` tag, or restore the backup
`/opt/sub2api/sub2api.bak.czc-v2026.10.22.1-<UTC timestamp>` and restart
`sub2api.service`. Without a binary change, set
`gateway.codex_full_synthesis: false` to restore the previous request shape, or
`gateway.codex_wire.profile: stable` to keep the older wire behavior.

## Known intentional divergences

- Synthesized permissions/skills text is generated from the device profile
  rather than copied from a live Codex home; skill file paths are intentionally
  omitted.
- Synthetic `update_plan` uses a compact schema.
- `client_metadata` order is deterministic per turn/session, not OS-random.
- One account still serves multiple downstream users; device identity is shared
  per account while each downstream conversation gets its own session/thread.
